notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079937/d0d8eedf7b5a2b5bd0da1ce93d025aa66b76c9d2.png

Hi everyone,

Please find below the changes brought by the 7th Early Access Major Update!

[previewyoutube=c_QFjamy270;full][/previewyoutube]

Adjusted Place Kicking Mechanic 
The place kick mechanic has been modified to make conversion and penalty goal kicks more challenging. After aiming, Right Stick down increases power, followed by Right Stick up for kick accuracy.

Added Tactics Selection
D-Pad now activates the tactics menu during gameplay. Up/Down on the D-Pad adjusts defensive tactics, Left/Right adjusts attacking tactics.

Added Team Management
Manage Lineup added to the pause menu to enable substitutions with a match. 

Added Quick Substitutions
A quick substitution menu has been added to the View button.

Added Tutorials
An initial pass of gameplay tutorials have been added, giving detail on the game mechanics, including Place Kicking, Scrums, Rucks, Mauls and Line Outs. 

Improved Gameplay
Gameplay has been polished/improved, including tweaking ruck steal timing and AI decision making. 

Improved Performance
The game has been further optimised to improve gameplay framerate, particularly on lower end machines.

Improved Stability 
This update features both general and Gameplay stability improvement.

Have fun on the pitch!

notes.title: Early Access 5 - Major Update
notes.content:
Dear players, 

We are happy to announce the release of Early Access 5, our Fifth Major Release during Rugby 25 early access period. 

Notes for what is included in this update are outlined below.

-----------

Improved Mauls
Mauls have been reworked in this update, improving animation fluidity as well as the gameplay experience.

Improved General Gameplay
Several general gameplay improvements have been made in addition to the ones added during the EA4 Interim Updates, these include improving the passing out of rucks, quick passes, catches, touch line avoidance and more.

Added URC Competition mode
The United Rugby Championship, including the 16 teams and 2024-25 fixtures, is now available in Competition mode. A number of these teams will feature photogrammetry visuals, with additional photogrammetry coming in future updates.

Added Stadiums
Several additional stadiums have been added in this update, including the officially licensed Cardiff Arms Park, Scotstoun, Kingspan Stadium, Swansea.com Stadium and Dexcom Stadium. Further MLR stadiums have also been added.

Added HUD Elements
A meter showing control over the ruck has been added, as well as HUD to identify those offside – both with an offside line shown during rucks and indicators on individual players.

Improved Graphics
Various tweaks have been made to the graphical appearance of the game, including work adjusting the grass, and various aspects of lighting and player detail.

Improved Stability
Several improvements to resolve non-progression issues during gameplay have been implemented in this update. 

We continue to appreciate reports to our support team to help us identify the remaining ones, via https://early.bigant.com/.

notes.content:
Hi everyone! Today we have a further interim update to the Early Access 2 release to share. After this, our next planned update will be the full launch of Early Access 3 late next week! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079937/cc1b4463ecf5b26de775521f052d875c9311a7be.png

Build notes for this update are as follows,
Tuned Passing
Passing remains an area heavily in development, in this update the AI will be more willing to make passes in gameplay, however it is a known issue that these occasionally result in some poor passes being made, on balance however we believe this is a better gameplay outcome than how the passing was in the previous update. 

In addition, this update includes further work to improve passing responsiveness for user-controlled players, as well as resolving cases where the ball wouldn’t be passed to the player indicated by the button prompts. 

Updated Animations
Several changes to animations have been implemented, including: 

 Changes to avoid high tackle animations being played when the tackle didn’t meet the conditions to be an illegal tackle
 Reduced delays in the in-play kicking animations 
 Improved general player positioning animations
 Various supporting changes for improving tackles, passing, rucks and mauls


Improved Stability
Numerous updates have been made to address reported issues in completing matches, thanks to everyone who has sent in support tickets to help us identify them, the various videos and helpful reproduction steps we received helped track a number of them down.

notes.content:

Hi Rugby fans! 

Welcome to the first major update in the Rugby 25 Early Access. Firstly, thanks for your support, patience, understanding, and, most of all, your generous feedback about the journey so far - it's been really helpful. Together we are building a great game!

Below you will find the notes for this release - we look forward to discussing the game and hearing what you think at forum.bigant.com

---


 Added Mauls
The initial maul mechanic has been added to the game, future updates will improve several of the animations around mauls to make them more visually fluid. 
Improved Tackles
A significant number of new tackle animations have been integrated, as well as adjustments to the underlying calculations for selecting which tackles to play.  The Dive Tackle control has been shifted to the Y button. 
Added Club Teams
A number of Gallagher Premiership and URC teams featuring initial photogrammetry based player visuals have been added. Over 100 players from the Ospreys, Dragons, Cardiff, Edinburgh, Connacht, Bath and Northampton Saints are now playable.

The officially licensed Allianz Stadium in Sydney has been added to the list of available stadiums, in addition to stadiums for Northampton, Parma, and Toulon.

The targeting of passes has been improved, with adjustments to the calculation for target selection and pass quality. 
Rebalanced rucks
The ruck system has been adjusted, improving the speeds of rucks and making them more of a contest, along with an alert for when a steal is available. 
Tuned Player Movement 
Initial work on balancing player run and sprint speeds has been done, the attributes and build of the player will have more impact on the speed they can run and the amount of boost that using the sprint button makes
Improved UI
Several UI screens have been given visual polish, notably the pre-match settings. A few in game elements, such as the player markers have also been polished.

A number of reported stability issues have been resolved, with work continuing to ensure all of those reported are found. Please continue to send them through.

notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079937/b6289594c5d9bebdea5cdb2efc6319a8496c4630.png

Hi Everybody! 

We're now well on the way towards the first Rugby 25 Major Update, which will release towards the end of July and will include improved rucks, mauls, tackling and more. In the meantime we have a few changes that we wanted to share early, in a third interim update released today. 

---


 Improved Passing
A first pass of ongoing work to improve passing has been made, this will improve the targeting of passes to better intersect players on a run, maintaining forward momentum better and reducing, but not eliminating wildly missed passes. Further refinement of passing remains a high priority of ours in upcoming updates. 
Resolved Incorrect Ruck Scoots
This update should reduce cases where the half would run forward through the ruck before being able to use the ball. 
Adjusted Kicking and Player Switch Controls
Based on feedback from the previous update, we have made a few changes to the controls scheme. The "Up and Under" and Punt kicks have been switched, so that Punt is now on the A button. Switching to the Full Back has been shifted from Y to LB+RB to avoid a common conflict with the Tackler Contest input in the ruck. 
Improved Camera
Adjustments have been made to the camera switching into gameplay after the conclusion of lineouts. 
Resolve Graphical Corruption
Ghosting effects present while playing with screen aspect ratios requiring letterboxing, such as a number of common handheld devices including the Steam Deck with a 16:10 aspect screen, have been resolved.

----

We look forward to receiving your feedback on this update at forum.bigant.com!

notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079937/45f370c6dd0237fc08b3dc1f4fa66b1ae60a02bb.jpg
Hi rugby fans! 

Our second interim update to the Early Access release of Rugby 25 is now available. We again thank everyone for their feedback, it has been valuable to the team and has shaped what we have worked on so far, as well as the priorities for future updates. 

Patch notes for this update are the following, 


 Improved Kicking
 In play kicks have been adjusted along with tuning of trajectories across all kick types. A dedicated button (A) has been implemented for Up and Under kicks.
Improved Offloads
Standard pass buttons may be used to offload in the early stages of a tackle. Note that offloads are more likely than standard passes to deviate from the target. This is an area on which we are hoping to get feedback to ensure we have balanced this correctly. 
Improved Scrum Half ruck join speed
The halves will attend rucks quicker to use the ball. The Ruck mechanic is still being worked on in response to feedback, this area of the game will have further improvement in future updates.
Corrected Rule implementation
Correction of some rules not implemented correctly, including the positioning of the lineout after free kicks to touch and ensuring defensive touchdowns are treated correctly.
Corrected unintentional forward passes
The logic for selecting a pass target when tapping LB/RB has been adjusted to avoid a small percentage of scenarios where the ball would be passed well forward to a teammate out of the ruck.

Stability improvements
A number of reported game stability issues have been rectified in this update, our support team thanks you! Please keep these reports coming through as they are encountered via https://early.bigant.com/

notes.title: Rugby 25 Early Access Roadmap
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079937/c64de63e1188434d380e38f3d410291df69bcd66.jpg
First of all, thank for your interest in Rugby 25 Early Access, we really appreciate you coming on board!

We appreciate all comments and critiques, the primary goal of Rugby 25 being in Early Access is to take the community on the development journey with us. 

We would like to clarify that this release of Rugby 25 Early Access has somewhat tuned graphics, for which the feedback has been overwhelmingly positive, and an early experimental build with regard to AI behaviours, for which you have let us know that we haven’t met the expected mark.

Today we are releasing a roadmap to indicate the major milestones that will occur over the next two months. In between these major updates, you will see frequent smaller updates from us as we tune the AI, improve animation and improve general stability.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2340870/Rugby_25/

This Early Access method is similar to that we have used to successfully bring TIEBREAK tennis to market, where features were basic at the start are worked upon with public consultation, even to the point of adding and removing gameplay mechanics.

We can only offer this flexibility and responsiveness by releasing the game in an early state, where the core rugby engine has been completed but now the AI and gameplay layers need to be added. You can expect regular updates from us, regular communication and regular additions to Rugby 25 Early Access. 

Rugby 25 has an unparalleled roster, far broader than that the sport has ever seen in a video game, and it is our aim to bring the gameplay up to that same level, this Early Access is merely the base from which we will build. We welcome and look forward to any feedback from you on Steam, or on the Big Ant forums to ensure Rugby 25 becomes the best Rugby ever made.

notes.title: Rugby 25 is now available in Early Access!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079937/354c26dcb3e06114a8641251b6e9cb7f915bfa29.jpg
At first look at this title, you might be wondering, 'Rugby 25? What happened to Rugby 24?' So let's dive right in.

First and foremost, we want to apologize for the significant wait you've endured over the past few years in anticipation of a new Rugby game. We've spent a considerable amount of time traveling the world to scan players from over 140 teams and sign various licensing agreements. While this is not an excuse, it may partially explain the delays.

Now that most of this phase is complete, we can now fully dedicate ourselves to developing the game and implementing the teams.

This Early Access phase will allow you to enjoy the game ahead of its full release, but also to influence the direction of its development. With promising feedback and a growing player base, Rugby 25 Early Access sets the stage for a groundbreaking entry into the world of rugby gaming, creating the most comprehensive Rugby video game of all time.

Upon Early Access release, teams will not be final, nor will the players have their photogrammetry likeness integrated into the game. As the Early Access period progresses, teams and players will have their names and likeness updated and integrated into the game.

It should be noted that the AI and player movement are in an experimental phase and anomalies will occur as we lock these important elements of the game in.

We expect delivery of the final version of Rugby 25 later in 2024, the exact length of the Early Access will be dependent upon feedback received and development progress.

[previewyoutube=v8zO97Mv7NU;full][/previewyoutube]
Early Access launch

Here we are! Rugby 25 is officially launching its Early Access!

In this initial Early Access release you will be able to select from 21 Nations, but the only team with cphotogrammetry will be the Australian Wallabies and French Teams. Other teams and photogrammetry will be constantly added as the Early Access period progresses.

Our goal with this Early Access is to eventually include:

●	Over 140 International Teams including New Zealand, South Africa, England, France and Australia.
●	Over 150 Club Sides
●	11 competitions, including URC, Gallagher Premiership, French Top 14 and Pro D2, MLR, and Super Rugby Pacific
●	A career mode: Navigate the highs and lows of a professional rugby coaching career. Build and manage your dream team, train players, develop strategies, and make crucial decisions to lead your team to victory
●	Rugby Academy: Create teams, players, logos and stadiums in the creation tools in Rugby24, make anything from your all-time favourite players to your local team.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079937/95c61e3c07df44efbbc26beca72d4395ff729c0b.png
Gameplay 

Let's talk gameplay now. We would like to remind you that we are still in the early stages of Rugby 25, but you can already expect these additions during Early Access:

- Realistic Gameplay: Experience the authentic feel of rugby with realistic physics and player movement, employing real rugby strategy to outplay your opponents.
- Dynamic Weather and Stadiums: Play in various weather conditions and iconic stadiums from around the world. Rain, mud, or shine, every match offers a unique challenge.
- Multiplayer actions: Challenge your friends or compete against players worldwide in cross platform online multiplayer modes. Show off your skills and climb the global leaderboards.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079937/08d5c34a98d6d275f9cefcb079a545df0c87fc78.png
Gameplay Modes 

From now on, you can start quick matches against an AI offline! During this Early Access period, we'll be adding new game modes such as :

- Exhibition Matches: Jump straight into the action with quick matches. Choose your teams, set the conditions, and get playing.
- Tournaments: Participate in major tournaments and leagues. Win trophies and achieve glory.
- Training: Hone your skills with dedicated tutorial training sessions. Practice different aspects of the game to perfect your technique.

Please note that this ‘roadmap’ isn't final, the content and timing are subject to change.

Want to closely follow the game's development?
